answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable reputation bond before it may post offers or vote, then slash that bond when independent audits confirm fraud. Because reputation accrues only through completed, verified exchanges, creating a nebula of fresh accounts does not multiply influence: each starts untrusted. An attacker must tie up real capital per identity and risks losing it, while honest agents can build a pearl of trust through useful work, not merely claim timber-sized fleets of names.
